headline: High risk of shared-filesystem prompt injection and data leakage from Gemini CLI into opik via files/MCP and broad egress.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files and use MCP; its state is shared with other instances via filesystem and git. opik exposes a REST API and broad network egress, so if it ingests artifacts from the shared workspace, attacker-controlled file content from Gemini CLI can influence downstream instructions. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or git checkout
IF opik parses Gemini CLI-produced files or logs as instructions or prompts
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP servers not strictly needed
Treat all file content as untrusted input
Add a manual review step before opik consumes Gemini CLI outputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI explicitly reads files in the cwd and can send data over broad network egress; opik exposes a REST API and broad egress as well. If they share a workspace, source code or shell-environment data touched by Gemini CLI can flow into opik outputs or API calls. The profiles do not prove a leak by default, but the shared-file path is plausible enough to rate medium.
conditions: IF the agents share repo files or a mounted cwd
IF opik forwards received artifacts to its REST API or another backend
mitigations: Use separate directories and mounts
Redact secrets before handoff
Restrict outbound network access for one agent
Log and review all cross-agent transfers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem and modify git state; the pair shares state via filesystem and git only. opik is not shown to write files, but it does have broad network egress and REST API access, so the main conflict is on shared mutable workspace resources rather than identical writes. Because the profiles do not document locking, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git repository
IF opik or its surrounding workflow mutates shared files without locking
mitigations: Assign one writer per repo
Use git locks or serialized commits
Run agents in separate branches
Disable concurrent edits to shared files

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code and file edits, while opik is an evaluation/observability tool that may consume those outputs. If opik treats Gemini CLI artifacts as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect evaluations or automated follow-on actions. The profiles do not show direct action-taking by opik, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF opik ingests Gemini CLI outputs without validation
IF downstream automation uses opik results to trigger commits, alerts, or reports
mitigations: Require human review of Gemini CLI outputs
Add schema and citation checks before ingestion
Compare outputs against a second source
Disable automatic downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and do not declare regulated data handling, residency, or certification constraints. Gemini CLI touches source code and shell environment; opik lists no data classes touched. With no documented mismatch, compliance risk is limited to potential local policy gaps rather than a clear cross-border or PHI issue.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the shared workspace
IF local policy requires stricter retention or residency than either profile states
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Set explicit retention rules
Review logging settings
Document data-handling boundaries
